info.title: Entitler keys service
info.description: Project keys: minting them from presets or scopes, listing, renaming, rotating and revoking them, and describing the key that sent a request. Organisation keys live on the projects service.

servers.description: For the dashboard: the session cookie and credentialed CORS.

key.description: A project key: a secret key starts `ent_test_` for a test environment or `ent_live_` for a live one, a publishable key `ent_pk_test_` or `ent_pk_live_`, then 32 letters and digits; keys minted before environments had kinds keep `ent_` alone. It names its project and environment and carries the scopes chosen when it was minted. Only a publishable key may send `Entitler-Identity-Token`.

orgKey.description: An organisation key, `ent_org_` and 32 letters and digits, with the scopes chosen when it was minted. It names the project and environment with the Entitler-Project and Entitler-Environment headers.

session.description: The access token `POST /auth/sign-in` returns on api.entitler.dev: a person, with the scopes of their role in the organisation of the project the request names.

sessionCookie.name: __Secure-entitler_session
sessionCookie.description: The same access token as an HttpOnly cookie, which api.entitler.app sets for the dashboard.

customerToken.description: A customer token from `POST /customers/{externalId}/tokens`: one customer, for at most an hour, with a subset of `entitlements:read`, `usage:read` and `usage:write`.

identityToken.name: Entitler-Identity-Token
identityToken.description: An identity token from a sign-in provider registered on the key's project, sent beside the key. It names the customer, `me`.

kind.description: `publishable` keys start `ent_pk_`, hold only product scopes and may send identity tokens; `secret` keys belong on a server.

rotatedAt.description: When the key last got a new token, or `null` if it never has.

previousTokenExpiresAt.description: When the token the key had before its last rotation stops working, which may have passed, or `null` if it stopped at the rotation or the key was never rotated.

next.description: Send it as `cursor` for the page after this one, or `null` on the last page.

projects.description: Sent for an `orgId` listing only: for each project, the keys counting against `api_keys` and its limit.

connectionId.description: The connection the listing sells through.

Channel.description: Where a listing sells: one of the environment's connections.

customer.description: The customer's external id the token names.

expiresAt.description: When the token stops being valid.

code.description: What went wrong, for code to act on.

payment.description: With `402 payment_required`: the payment a plan change waits on. The customer keeps their plan until it succeeds.

listingGaps.description: With `409 listing_gaps`: the gaps a rollout or experiment start would leave.

listingProblems.description: With `409 listing_invalid`: the listings whose Stripe price fails the checks.

kind.description: `secret` for a server, `publishable` for code that ships to browsers and devices, which holds only product scopes and starts `ent_pk_`. A preset chooses it: `pricing_page` and `app` are publishable, `server` and `management` secret; sending another kind with a preset is refused. Without either, a key holding only product scopes is publishable and any other secret.
`publishable` keys start `ent_pk_`, hold only product scopes and may send identity tokens; `secret` keys belong on a server.

previousTokenHours.description: How many hours the token being replaced keeps working alongside the new one, from 0 to 168. 0, the default, stops it at once.

kind.description: `publishable` for a key starting `ent_pk_`; `secret` for any other project key and for organisation keys.

registration.description: Sent with an identity token only: whether its provider lets a subject it has not seen register itself.

kind.description: `stops_selling`: the track sells it on the channel today and the new catalogue leaves it blank there. `unlisted`: a self-serve plan and period with no ids on any of the environment's connections. An environment with no connection has no gaps.

ListingGap.description: A plan and billing period a listing leaves blank. Sales-led plans never have gaps.

problem.description: `price_not_found` when the Stripe connection has no such price, `price_inactive` when it is archived, `interval_mismatch` when it bills on another interval than the billing period, or recurs for a one-time plan.

status.description: Why the payment has not succeeded: the card was declined, the customer must confirm it (such as 3D Secure), the provider is still processing it, or the provider gave no reason.

url.description: The provider's page where the customer pays or confirms it, or null.

needsManagementKeys.description: Whether a key holding it needs `management_keys`. Reading and changing customers and minting their tokens are refused from a web page like any management scope, but need no `management_keys`.

get.summary: Describe the key that sent the request
get.description: Its id, name, organisation, project, environment, scopes, allowed origins and times; never the hash or the plaintext. A session is answered 404, because it is not a key. Sent with an identity token beside a project key, `scopes` lists the scopes that pair holds: the key's scopes that the token's provider allows and an identity may hold, from `entitlements:read`, `usage:read`, `usage:write` and `customers:register`. `registration` then says whether the provider lets a person it has not seen register. A token the project's providers cannot verify is refused with 401. A customer token is answered with the customer it names, its scopes and when it expires; one that is not valid now is refused with 401.

get.description: The project's keys, masked, or with `orgId` those of every project in the organisation, a page of up to 100 at a time in the order they were created. Revoked keys are left out unless `includeRevoked` is `true`; the keys of a deleted environment stay listed until they are revoked. `used` counts the keys not revoked in the project's live environments, whichever environment the caller's key is in, so it matches the count `api_keys` limits. With `orgId`, `projects` gives that count and the limit for each project.

post.description: In the project and environment the request names, from a preset, a list of scopes or both, with optional allowed origins. A publishable key (the `pricing_page` and `app` presets, or `kind: "publishable"`) starts `ent_pk_test_` or `ent_pk_live_` and holds only product scopes; a secret key starts `ent_test_` in a test environment and `ent_live_` in a live one. The plaintext comes back once; a replay returns the key without it. A key holds only scopes its minter holds in its environment, after the environment's protection, and one with a management scope other than `customers:read`, `customers:write` and `tokens:mint` needs `management_keys`.

patch.summary: Rename a project key or change its scopes
patch.description: Changes the name, the scopes or both of a key that is not revoked; its token stays the same. A publishable key keeps to product scopes. Changing the scopes needs a caller holding every scope the key has in its environment, and the new scopes follow the rules for minting: only scopes the caller holds there, and a management scope other than `customers:read`, `customers:write` and `tokens:mint` needs `management_keys`. The keys service applies a change at once and every other service within about 30 seconds.

post.description: Gives a key that is not revoked a new token, keeping its id, name, scopes and allowed origins; the new token starts as the old one did, by the key's kind and its environment's. The plaintext comes back once; a replay returns the key without it. The token it replaces stops working at once, or after `previousTokenHours` so you can update everything that uses it; other services may accept it for about 30 seconds longer. Only a caller holding every scope of the key in its environment can rotate it, and a key with a management scope other than `customers:read`, `customers:write` and `tokens:mint` needs `management_keys`.
